clue.text: Vulgar jerk on the march

indicators.note: in a down-to-earth sense one piece sits on, i.e. after, the other in the answer

parts.note: a protest march is a demo
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A coarse fellow twitches as he takes part in a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for the vulgar person, but it is the twitch; 'on' sets it after the march word, as one piece follows another.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic language is that of ordinary people, so popular and common, hence vulgar in its old sense.

clue.text: Remark to disparage son put inside

indicators.note: says the son's letter is placed within the word for disparaging

parts.note: to decry something is to disparage it

explanation.surface: Someone makes a cutting comment to belittle a boy who has been jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remark' is not a comment here but re-mark, to notice: S goes inside DECRY.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is to catch sight of, and remark in its older sense means to notice or observe.

clue.text: Speaker, in the end, overturned suspensions

indicators.note: places the speaker inside the overturned goal
in a down clue the word for goal is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A speaker, finally toppled, sees the proceedings suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' reads as 'finally', but 'the end' is a goal; 'overturned' turns it up in this down clue, giving MIA, and 'in' holds the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria is the plural of moratorium, a temporary suspension or ban on an activity.

clue.text: Debate raised about amount of interest in drinking place

indicators.note: the reversed debate word goes around the interest rate
in a down clue the debate word is lifted up, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to moot is to raise for debate
APR, annual percentage rate, measures the interest on a loan

explanation.surface: An argument flares up over interest rates in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the debate word to TOOM in this down clue, and 'about' wraps it around the lender's interest rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproom is the bar of a pub or inn where drinks are served from the tap.

clue.text: Makes applications for the preservation of woods

definitions.text: Makes applications for the preservation of woods

parts.words: Makes applications for the preservation of woods
parts.note: reads like someone lodging requests to protect forests, but means painting timber with a tarry preservative

explanation.surface: A campaigner files requests to save the forests.
explanation.definitionFit: This tar oil is brushed onto fences and sheds to stop the timber rotting, each coat an application.

clue.text: One who may choose a German prince

definitions.meaning: a voter, someone entitled to choose in an election
one of the princes of the Holy Roman Empire entitled to choose the emperor

explanation.surface: A German prince is the one who gets to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter in an election, and also a title for German princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor.

clue.text: English law about parking upheld, so drive out

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is held up, so its letters read backwards
the law word goes around the parking letter

parts.note: lex is Latin for law, familiar from legal phrases
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Under English law, a parking offence is upheld and the offender is ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts P inside LEX to make LEPX, and 'upheld' turns that to XPEL after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone is to force them out, to drive them away.

clue.text: Note on Gaelic version of mournful song

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: a version of the word is a reworked form of its letters

explanation.surface: A singer adds a note to a Gaelic lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaelic' looks like a description of the song; 'version' makes its letters LEGIAC, placed after the note.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem or song, and elegiac describes anything belonging to one.

clue.text: More natural time to mourn the king

parts.note: to rue is to regret or lament
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: It is only right that it is time to grieve for the dead king.
explanation.definitionFit: Truer means more genuine or faithful, nearer to the real thing, as in true to life.

clue.text: Slowing down. out of pique, initially, being discontented

indicators.note: taken as framing the slowing word around the letter taken from pique

parts.note: reining a horse in slows it down

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of pique

explanation.surface: Someone slackens pace in a fit of pique, feeling sorry for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: P, the first letter of 'pique', goes inside REINING; the setter leaves the insertion loosely signalled.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or complain, so repining means feeling and voicing discontent.

clue.text: Battle with dilapidated car nothing on it's any good

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
a heap is slang for a battered old car

explanation.surface: A punch-up breaks out over a wrecked car that is worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a pile of discarded junk, where everything is thought useless.

clue.text: Stock English joke

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: An Englishman tells a hackneyed gag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like an adjective for the joke; it is the verb, to furnish.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock a place is to supply or furnish it with what it needs.

clue.text: Relation helping anonymously?

indicators.note: anonymous means without a name, and N is the abbreviation for name, so that letter goes

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: A relative who helps out without seeking credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' wants to be a family member; it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the quantitative relation between two amounts.

clue.text: Private cricket side continue doggedly

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A soldier in the cricket team keeps plugging away.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to persevere through difficulty, as a soldier presses forward.

clue.text: Given term, inmate can reform — he got support from home

indicators.note: to reform is to re-form, giving the letters a new shape

explanation.surface: A prisoner handed a sentence may yet mend his ways, and his family supports him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' looks like the prisoner going straight, but it shuffles TERM INMATE CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A man sent abroad by his British family and living on money they posted to keep him away.

clue.text: Feeling of warmth produced by disease

definitions.meaning: an old medical sense, a condition affecting part of the body

explanation.surface: Fondness can come from illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Means fondness, and in medical use a morbid condition, as in an affection of the lungs.

clue.text: Pins very obviously protrude from this garment

definitions.text: Pins very obviously protrude from this garment

parts.words: Pins very obviously protrude from this garment
parts.note: pins is slang for legs, which show plainly below a very short skirt

explanation.surface: A dressmaker has left the pins sticking out of a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A very short skirt ending well above the knee leaves the legs on show.

clue.text: Lifting up motorway fence and running through

indicators.note: in a down clue the motorway's letters are raised, so read backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
a paling is a fence of pointed stakes

explanation.surface: Workers raise a motorway fence and run along it.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is England's London-to-Leeds motorway; 'Lifting up' turns MI to IM.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce with a sharp stake, so running a body through.

clue.text: Naked ladies producing bother in stables — endless outrage

indicators.note: puts the bother word inside the stables word

parts.note: mews were originally stables round a yard
ado means fuss or bother

indicators.note: the last letter of the outrage word is cut off

parts.note: an affront is an insult or outrage

explanation.surface: Nude women cause a stir in the stables, an outrage without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naked ladies' is a folk name for the autumn crocus, which flowers without leaves; 'endless' cuts AFFRONT to AFFRON.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is called naked ladies because its flowers appear on bare stems with no leaves.

clue.text: Cosmos is almost entirely the result of diffusion

indicators.note: all but the first letter of these words is used, the run sitting within them

explanation.surface: The universe is said to have spread out from one point.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the C of 'Cosmos is' and the rest reads straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the passage of a solvent through a membrane, a form of diffusion.

clue.text: Good relations with one side on board after strike

indicators.note: puts the side of the ship after the strike in the answer

parts.note: to rap is to hit sharply
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: Getting along with the crew after a punch-up aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious understanding between people.

clue.text: Familiar china

definitions.meaning: an intimate associate, someone well known to one
Cockney rhyming slang, china plate for mate

explanation.surface: Familiar porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar is a close companion, and china in rhyming slang is a mate.

clue.text: Sort of gun requiring no trigger?

definitions.meaning: a firearm that keeps firing while the trigger is held
happening by itself, with nothing needed to set it off

explanation.surface: A gun that fires without anyone pulling the trigger.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a self-loading firearm, and anything that works by itself without prompting.

clue.text: Sort of wood obtainable from north

indicators.note: the letters of the next word can be rearranged to obtain the tree

explanation.surface: A kind of timber comes from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn and blackthorn are trees and their timber, thorn wood.

clue.text: All families have these boxes, for instance

definitions.meaning: family ..., the charts of a family's descent
box is an evergreen shrub or small tree

explanation.surface: Every family keeps boxes like these.
explanation.definitionFit: Every family has a family tree, and box is one kind of tree.

clue.text: To get a sitter can be a problem

definitions.meaning: one who sits for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: Finding someone to sit for a portrait can be tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: One who poses is a model or sitter, and a poser is also a baffling question.

clue.text: Flattens with metal spades

definitions.meaning: presses smooth, as clothes with a hot iron
golf clubs with metal heads, one older one being called a spade mashie

explanation.surface: Someone levels the ground with steel shovels.
explanation.definitionFit: To press smooth is to iron, and golf clubs with metal heads include the spade mashie.

clue.text: Illustrate version of poem — it is English

indicators.note: a version of these letters is a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Someone illustrates their own translation of a poem, noting it is in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' shuffles POEM, IT IS and E together.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise is to typify or be a perfect example of, so to illustrate something.

clue.text: It includes the first week's accounts

definitions.text: It includes the first week's accounts

parts.words: It includes the first week's accounts
parts.note: sounds like a ledger for a new business, but means the Bible book telling the six days of creation and the day of rest

explanation.surface: A new firm's ledger covers its opening week.
explanation.definitionFit: The first book of the Bible gives the account of the world being made in seven days.

clue.text: Provided musical guidance, getting approval round the gallery

indicators.note: the approval word goes round the gallery name

parts.note: a nod signals approval
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A conductor gives directions and wins approval at the art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is London's best-known art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Notated music is written down in notation, the marks that guide a performer.
